events.title: “The Promise: Untold Stories of SC’s African American Patriots” Dinner Theatre followed by a Revolutionary Conversation
events.description:
“The Promise: Untold Stories of South Carolina’s African American Patriots” is rooted in real history of 1700s America, according to one of the writers of the stage production.

Annette Dees Grevious, along with Brandi LaShay, are writers for the Claflin Theatre Ensemble production highlighting the experiences of six Black men captured by the British in Charleston as they attempt to escape and claim the pensions they were promised.

The play explores themes of freedom, survival and the overlooked contributions of African Americans during early-American conflicts. Through dramatized storytelling, the production brings attention to the struggles and resilience of enslaved individuals who sought liberation and recognition for their service.

While the play includes dramatic license to weave together a narrative, Grevious said one of the most meaningful aspects of the production is the connection to real history, even when documentation is limited.

“Each of these men are real men, and although it may not have been exactly their story, due to lack of documentation, it was definitely some Black person’s story. And this production gets to share and uplift those that are able to view it,” Grevious said.

Following the performance, a Revolutionary Conversation will allow for small group and communal sharing about the tough subjects involved in the play.

“We wanted to create a safe space after each performance because it can be a sensitive subject for viewers, so being able to allow the audience to ask questions and get clarity or share knowledge with one another is beneficial,” she said.

The production aims to educate audiences while honoring the untold stories of African American patriots whose contributions have often been left out of historical narratives.

The production was sponsored in part by the Orangeburg County Chamber of Commerce and a grant from SC250. This performance of the play is part of the SC American Revolution Sestercentennial Commission (SC250)’s Q2 Commission Meeting events.

The dinner theater and conversation are free and open to the public. However, reservations are required no later than November 2, 2026.

events.title: The Promise: Untold Stories of SC’s Black Patriots
events.description: Set during the Revolutionary War, Six Black Patriots from South Carolina are captured by British forces during the Siege of Charleston; a pivotal battle that serves as a victory for the British and Loyalist forces. As the pressure of captivity intensifies, the soldiers are left behind only to realize a broader struggle that will determine their fate. Will their promise of freedom, liberty, and life be in the hands of the Continental Army, or will the British Crown rule?

events.title: Lunch & Learn: The Charleston Patriots: Strangers in a Strange Land
events.description:
A few months after the surrender of Charles Town in 1780 the British rounded up and arrested sixty-three of the most prominent leaders of the Revolutionary movement in South Carolina despite pledging on their honor that they would not violate the terms of their parole. They were sent to East Florida where they were held against their will under town arrest in St. Augustine as prisoners of war for 9 months.

Robert Ryals returns to the Rev War Visitor Center to share this dramatic and sometimes amusing historic storytelling experience based on the diary and experiences of Josiah Smith, a Charles Town merchant.

RSVP @ simplyrevolutionary.com

You bring your lunch and we will provide the learning opportunity!

events.title: Screening of “Our Story, Too: Women, Native Americans and African Americans in the Revolutionary War.”
events.description:

It was produced by SCETV with production funding provided by the South Carolina American Revolution Sestercentennial Commission (SC250).

events.description: A lecture by historian and battlefield preservationist Durant Ashmore. The Fall of Savannah in December 1778 was one of the ten most important strategic events of the Revolutionary War. Come find out why.

events.title: First Blood: The First Siege of Ninety Six
events.description: A lecture by historian and battlefield preservationist Durant Ashmore. At the first Siege of Ninety Six (November 19–21, 1775), James Birmingham was killed, the first South Carolinian to die in the name of Liberty. Durant discusses the events that led to his death.

events.title: Revolutionary War Review Homeschool Friday – SC Revolutionary Leaders
events.description:

Come and learn about some of South Carolina’s Revolutionary Leaders such as Robert Anderson, Andrew Pickens, Henry Laurens, Thomas Sumter, Francis Marion, Thomas Heyward, Jr., Arthur Middleton, and others.

As a part of our celebrations and remembrances during the 250th, the Anderson County Museum is adding a series to our Homeschool Friday program.

The Revolutionary War Review series will focus on several elements of the Revolutionary War and is open to all students.

events.title: Remember the Ladies: Backcountry
events.description:
Spend your morning with some of the Patriot ladies of South Carolina’s backcountry.
Program Highlights:

  • Colonel Rawdon, Commander of the Camden Garrison, will spar with Mrs. Sarah McCalla over her husband being held as a POW.
  • Paul Wood will speak on Dicey Langston and her Revolutionary legacy.
  • Bettise Davidson will tell the story of the Widow Jenkins of Marion District who defied a British officer.

Light refreshments will be served.

*After our program, visitors are encouraged to visit Historic Camden for a “Make & Take” craft for the ladies.*

events.title: Van Tour: The First and Second Cherokee Wars
events.description:
A van tour with historian and battlefield preservationist Durant Ashmore to sites of the first and second Cherokee Wars: Fort Prince George, Keowee, Eastatoe, Tomassee, Esseneca and Fort Rutledge. The Cherokees chose some of the most beautiful places in the state for their towns, so come enjoy the fall foliage as we study these tragic wars.

The tour leaves from Greenville; meeting spot and end time to be announced. For details and reservations, contact Durant Ashmore on Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/durant.ashmore

events.title: Revolutionary Art: A Conversation with the South Carolina State House Tour Office
events.description: Join the South Carolina State Library for a special event, Revolutionary Art: A Conversation with the South Carolina State House Tour Office. Staff from the South Carolina State House Tour Office will discuss the history and significance of the paintings in the South Carolina State House, including important battles and scenes from the American Revolution in South Carolina. They will also provide resources from various South Carolina State Parks and Historic Sites, highlighting Revolutionary War history throughout the state.

events.title: Revolutionary War Review Homeschool Friday – Battle of Eutaw Springs
events.description:
December 4 – The Battle of Eutaw Springs, SC (September 8, 1781).

We will be looking at the Battle of Eutaw Springs, SC, that was fought on September 8, 1781. We’ll go over the various military units and leaders engaged in the fight as we examine the facts of the battle before, during, and after. Then, we will track how this impacted the larger course of the war.

As a part of our celebrations and remembrances during the 250th, the Anderson County Museum is adding a series to our Homeschool Friday program.

The Revolutionary War Review series will focus on several elements of the Revolutionary War and is open to all students.

events.title: Behind Enemy Lyrics
events.description: Join Rev. John Paul Marr at the Anderson County Museum as we explore the revolutionary warfare of words. 18th century broadsheet lyrics functioned as part of the ideological propaganda machine for both the British and the Patriots. The stories of these songs and their rippling effects provide another perspective for understanding the founding of the United States of America. Hear the tunes and experience the back-and-forth battles of singing the songs of the American Revolution.

events.title: Eliza – An American Opera
events.description:
ELIZA: A Chamber Opera brings to life the courage, enterprise, and resilience of free, enslaved, and freed African and African-descended market women in relationship with Jewish Femme Soles in Revolutionary-era Charleston, South Carolina.

Commissioned by the Jonathan Green Maritime Cultural Center at the University of South Carolina Beaufort and sponsored in part by the SC250 Commission, the opera explores women’s roles in commerce, community, and the pursuit of freedom.
